args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money, per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail on `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` (e.g. `2.665` rounded up to `2.67` instead of the correct `2.66`).

## Changes
- Replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`, matching the existing docstring and FIN-212.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed.
args.head: fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212

transcript.content: I'll start by looking at the current state of the repository and the failing test.
The docstring already says banker's rounding but the code uses `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I'll create a branch and fix it.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Note: 2.675 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN quantize gives 2.68? Decimal("2.675") quantize 0.01 with HALF_EVEN: 2.675 -> digit is 7, last kept digit is 7 (odd) -> rounds to 2.68. Yes. 2.665 -> last kept digit 6 (even), tie -> 2.66. So ROUND_HALF_EVEN passes.

Create branch, commit fix, run CI, then PR.
